package_info.why_malicious: The report summarizes multiple malware campaigns and attack types (banking trojans, remote access malware, ransomware, DDoS, credential stealers, bootkits), but does not provide specific package-level details or code samples for any single malicious software package. Therefore, no single package can be analyzed at the required granularity.

behavioral_signatures: Banking trojans that overlay or interact with legitimate financial apps
Fake security update prompts leading to malware installation
Remote access malware disguised as anti-spyware tools
Ransomware encrypting files and demanding payment
Credential stealers targeting gaming or financial accounts
file_indicators: APK files mimicking legitimate banking or security apps
Malicious executables named after security tools
Unexpected modifications to Windows Boot Manager or UEFI partitions
network_indicators: Connections to known C2 infrastructure for banking trojans, ransomware, or credential stealers
Exfiltration of credentials or financial data to attacker-controlled servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of applications from unofficial sources, especially those mimicking financial or security apps. Detect overlays or accessibility service abuse on Android. Watch for suspicious network connections to known C2 domains, and for attempts to modify bootloader or UEFI partitions. Use endpoint protection to identify known malware signatures and behaviors.
